correctness.rationale: The greedy bridge lemma gives an exact characterization of each minimal absent word. For run lengths at least two, every ready state at run j has precisely the opposite-next (+1 run) and same-next (+2 run) continuations, both preserving readiness; terminal ready counts 2 and 3, and the two initial letters contribute Fibonacci-adjacent counts. The proof covers all positive k and all a,b>=2; direct enumeration and bridge enumeration agree on 25 finite cases, with 4056 additional graph/Fibonacci tests.

value.rationale: Minimal absent scattered subsequences form the finite antichain basis for the omitted subsequence language, relevant to loss-tolerant string observation and piecewise-testable constraints. The theorem exactly counts the complete antichain for a two-parameter infinite family, exhibits unexpected insensitivity to both positive run weights beyond one, and identifies Fibonacci growth in repetition count. A general enumeration algorithm does not itself explain this structural transition; the count is not a single instance or routine finite recomputation.
